solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

Q051-01.notes: Slope = -6/4 = -3/2; y-3 = -3/2(x-2) -> 3x+2y=12. All four choices pass through (2,3) (no shortcut); B slope -2/3 (reciprocal), C slope 3/2 (sign), D slope 2/3. Good distractors.

Q051-03.notes: Solve first two: x=3, y=1. 3k+3=13 -> k=10/3. Routine; graphing first two lines gives (3,1) immediately.

Q051-04.notes: 45o = 2(30b) -> o = 4b/3; 7b/3 = 630 -> b = 270, o = 360. D (360) is the orchestra-count trap; C is half of 630.

Q051-06.notes: L-10 = W+10 = s, so (s+10)(s-10)=525 -> s^2=625. Equivalently W=15, L=35, side 25. Difference-of-squares insight optional; quadratic route routine.

flags: minor: similar in style to official SAT items on rational functions defined for all real x (discriminant < 0), but not a close copy
Q051-07.notes: Need x^2-6x+k with no real zeros: 36-4k<0 -> k>9; least integer 10. Trap: 9 (gives double root at x=3).

Q051-09.notes: t + 1.2t = 220 wpm -> t = 100. C (120) is Rachel's rate; B (110) is the even split; D = 1.2*110.

Q051-10.notes: (1/3)pi(2r)^2(12) = pi r^2 h -> h = 16. D=48 omits 1/3; B=8 forgets to square 2; A=4 ignores radius ratio. Good distractors.

Q051-11.notes: Legs 2 and 1, hyp sqrt5: sin^2=4/5, cos^2=1/5, difference 3/5. B (1) is the Pythagorean-identity trap; D (3) omits hypotenuse; C = sinA+cosA.

Q051-12.notes: 80 > 78 raises A's mean; removing 80 < 83 from B raises B's mean. B must have other students since its mean is 83 != 80. Trap B (assuming leaving lowers B's mean).
